Other builders are editing these parts now: find everything by function name, not line number. DECISIONS 1. One new change action, `keep_running`, with a `do` argument (keep | restart | stop). No new argument on start_model / stop_model / restart_model: each is a locked workflow whose version hashes its run, schema and description (three validated versions would go back to "needs validation"), test/change.test.mjs pins restart_model's argument list exactly, and their rails are model rails (library model, port 8000, test prompt, `spark.console=1`). keep_running is NOT a workflow (no WORKFLOWS entry, lock or validation). The five workflow versions must be identical before and after this change; if one moved, a listed function was edited by mistake. 2. An app is described by `container`, `image`, `port` ("host:inside"), `volumes` (named Docker volumes only), `env` (NAME=value, no secrets), `memoryGB`. Never GPU, host folders, host network, privileged, a command override or a Docker restart policy. 3. Link = `http://:`. tsip is the Spark's own `tailscale ip -4` (inventory). Host port is the `port` argument, else the first TCP port `docker port` shows bound to 0.0.0.0, :: or tsip. Check = one GET / from the console; any HTTP reply counts. 4. Spark 2: `notBrainsSpark([spark])` is the first guard for every verb; `spark` is required so nothing is placed unnamed; `desiredAfter` already drops brain Sparks. 5. Image: owner-named, no trusted list. It runs at once only for the owner on their tailnet (page, POST /actions, own Sparkie chat with image, port, volumes and env all in their words). Anything else is one button that shows them all; from an agent, Telegram, an internet session or a saved step it is an owner-only button (the `undo_update` pattern). 6. Should-be-running = `desired.json` entries with `app: true`. Healing = `healPass` -> `healApp` -> `runAction('keep_running')` via watcher (docker start only). 7. Job types reused: `deploy` (new container, with `model: container`), `restart`, `stop`. No new job or event type. A. service/src/05-library.mjs and 24-handler.mjs - INVENTORY_SCRIPT, after the `deploy` line (same tab style): `docker ps -a --format 'ctr\t{{.Names}}\t{{.State}}' 2>/dev/null`. - `inventory()`: each Spark gets `containers: fields(r.out, 'ctr').map(([name, state]) => ({ name, state }))`. - GET /models: send `sparks: inv.sparks.map(({ containers, ...sp }) => sp)` (members read it). B. New part service/src/21-apps.mjs Constants: `APP_ANSWER_MS = Number(process.env.SPARK_CONSOLE_APP_ANSWER_MS || 180000)`, `APP_MEMORY_GB = 4`, `SECRET_NAME = /KEY|TOKEN|SECRET|PASSW|CREDENTIAL|AUTH/i`. Functions: - `appAnswers(host, port, timeout = 4000)`: http GET /, resolves true on any response (`res.resume()`), or on an error whose code starts `HPE_`; else false. Never rejects, keeps no body. - `appLook(node, container, tsip)`: one `run` (20 s) printing `protect\t`, then `docker port NAME 2>/dev/null | while IFS= read -r l; do printf 'port\t%s\n' "$l"; done`, then `echo looked`. No `looked` line or code != 0: 409 " didn't answer just now. Try again." Parse `^(\d+)/tcp -> (.*):(\d+)$` (strip [ ]). Returns `{ protect, open, closed }`: open = first with ip in 0.0.0.0, ::, tsip; closed = first other. - `appRoom(node, gb, container)`: `memNow(node)`; null -> 409 "Free memory on can't be read right now, so nothing was started (it could freeze the Spark)."; `available - KEEP_FREE < gb * 2**30` -> 409 " doesn't have room for now: it may use up to GB, and GB is free beyond the 8 GB kept for the system. Nothing was started. Stop a model there, pick another Spark, or say a smaller memory figure." - `appRunCommand(a, tsip)`: `docker run -d --name C --label spark.app=1 --restart no --memory g --log-opt max-size=50m --log-opt max-file=3 -p 127.0.0.1:H:I [-p tsip:H:I when tsip != 127.0.0.1] [-v each] [-e each] IMAGE`, every token through `q()`. - `appUp(job, node, container, host, port)`: every 3 s until APP_ANSWER_MS: `job.checkPause()`; `docker inspect -f '{{.State.Status}}'`; not running -> throw " stopped right after starting.\n"; with a port, `appAnswers` true -> return; with no port, 5 running looks in a row -> return; timeout -> throw " is running but didn't answer at port

within minutes. container_logs shows what it's doing." - `appNamed(input, saidText)` (intent gate): every word of `tokensOf(container)` (at least one) is in the owner's words (`said.has` or in `squash`ed text). If `knowledge.workloads[spark/container]` exists and isn't removed, or do is restart/stop: true unless they named Sparks and not this one. Otherwise (new app): `said.has(spark)`, image present, and image, each volume and each env appear verbatim (lowercased) in the words, and each number of `port` is a said token. - `appNow(x, sp, busy, check)`: `c = sp?.containers?.find(name)`; `link = sp?.tsip && x.port ? http://tsip:port : null`; returns `{...x, kind: 'app', link, state}`: running (plus `answers` when check and link), else changing when busy, else held with why: Spark not reachable / "its container is gone" / last heal-skipped why / exit 255 words / "it isn't running". - `healApp(x, inv)`: return when Spark offline or no `c`; running -> `skippedOnce.delete`, return; `consoleStopped` within 15 min -> return; watcher `w.oomKilled` -> healSkip. `back = cameBack(spark)`, `last = max(healCount('back:'+key))`, `seen` = newest stopped/crashed event for it. power = back && back.on > last && now - back.on < HEAL_WINDOW && seen.at >= back.off && seen.at <= back.on + 5 min; power and now - back.on < HEAL_SETTLE_MS -> return. crashed = w && !w.running && exitCode not null and not 0/137/143. Neither -> return (a clean stop with the Spark on is someone's stop: held). `healCount >= 2` -> healSkip "it was brought back twice in the last 6 hours already". Else healMark, fleetEvent healing with why " came back on" or "it stopped by itself (exit N)", then `runAction('keep_running', healOwner(), {spark, container}, {actor:'Self-healing', via:'watcher', request, canChange:true, trusted:true})`. No operation and outcome not already/kept, or a throw -> heal-skipped "bringing it back failed: ". - `action({ name: 'keep_running', title: 'Keep an app running', kind: 'change', scope: 'fleet:act', who: 'owner', destructive: true, ... })`. Schema (additionalProperties false, required spark and container): `spark` sparkArg; `container` string `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,62}$`; `do` string enum keep/restart/stop; `image` string maxLength 300 `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._/-]{0,200}(:[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127})?(@sha256:[a-f0-9]{64})?$`; `port` string `^[0-9]{2,5}(:[0-9]{2,5})?$`; `volumes` array maxItems 4 of string maxLength 260 `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_.-]{0,62}:/[A-Za-z0-9_./-]{1,190}$`; `env` array maxItems 12 of string maxLength 300 `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,63}=[^\n\r]{0,230}$`; `memoryGB` integer 1 to 32. No `choice`, no approval arguments. Description: "Use when the owner asks to keep an app or service that isn't a model running (Open WebUI, a database, any container), or to restart or stop one kept that way. A container already on that Spark joins the list of what should be running (should_be_running): Spark Console starts it again if it stops by itself or its Spark is powered off and on. With image and port, for one that isn't there yet, it starts it first (no GPU, opened on your tailnet only). do "restart" restarts it; do "stop" stops it and takes it off the list. It gives the link to open it at and whether it answers. Never on Sparkie's Spark, never a model (start_model, stop_model and restart_model are for those), never a protected container. Starting a new image may come back as a question for the owner." run(input, viewer, ctx), guards in this order: 1. verb = do || 'keep'; verb != keep with image/port/volumes/env/memoryGB -> 400 "With do restart or stop, give only spark and container." 2. `notBrainsSpark([spark])`; `sparkOf`; `mustUse`. 3. `inv = await inventory(null)`; Spark offline -> 409 " isn't reachable right now." 4. in `sp.deployments` -> 409 " is one of Spark Console's models. Models are started, stopped and restarted with start_model, stop_model and restart_model, and are already kept running." 5. verb != stop and (in `sp.external` or the watcher's `servedModels` non-empty) -> 409 " serves models, so it isn't kept running as an app: memory for a model is checked by start_model." 6. `appLook`; `isProtected(container, look.protect)` -> 403 " is protected." 7. state = `sp.containers` entry's state or 'missing'; entry = desired app entry; gb = memoryGB || entry.memoryGB || 4; hostPort = port's host part, else look.open.host, else entry.port. 8. stop / restart with no entry -> 409 " on isn't an app Spark Console keeps running, so there's nothing to here." 9. stop: `claimed([spark], 'stopping ', () => newJob('stop', {node, container, app:true, by, actor, via, request}))`; body `pausedCheck(ctx); await stopContainer(j, spark, container, viewer); await stoppedForSure(j, spark, container)`. Returns started, with note "It comes off the list of what should be running, so it stays stopped. Its container and data are kept." 10. restart: missing -> 404 " is on the list, but its container is gone from . To start it again, say which image to run and the port to open it at."; running -> job `restart` running `docker restart --time 20`, then appUp (on failure leave it running); not running -> step 12. 11. keep, running: when not listed or port/memoryGB changed call `keepApp`; return `{outcome: 'kept' | 'already', spark, container, link, answers, note}` with no operation. Notes: " on is now on the list of what should be running: Spark Console starts it again if it stops by itself or is powered off and on." / " on is already kept running; nothing changed." plus one of " It answers at ." / " Its link is , but it isn't answering there right now." / " No published port is known for it, so there's no link: say its port." / " Its port

isn't opened on 's tailnet address, so it has no link from your other devices." 12. keep (or restart), exists but stopped: appRoom; keepApp if listed and port/memory changed; `claimed` + `newJob('restart', {node, container, app:true, port: hostPort, memoryGB, ...})`; body: pausedCheck, `docker start`, `consoleStopped.delete`, appUp; on any failure or cancel set consoleStopped, `docker stop --time 20`, note "It didn't come up, so it was stopped again. Its container is kept, so its log can be read.", rethrow. On success with a port: `j.endpoint = link`, note "It answers at ". 13. keep, missing: no image -> 404 "There's no container called on . To start a new app there, say which image to run and the port to open it at."; no port -> 400 "Missing argument: port (where to open it, like "3000:8080")."; name starts `sc-` or equals a library model name -> 400 "That name is one of Spark Console's models. Pick another name for the app."; host port outside 1024-65535 or equal to CONFIG.servePort -> 400 "The port to open it at has to be between 1024 and 65535, and not (Spark Console's models answer there)."; an env whose name matches SECRET_NAME or that `maskSecrets` would change -> 400 " looks like a key, token or password. Spark Console doesn't pass secrets to an app: set it on the app's own page."; no tsip -> 409 "'s tailnet address isn't known right now, so the app can't be opened on your tailnet only. Try again in a minute."; then `ownerHere = ['page','api','sparkie'].includes(ctx.via) && !viewer.session && !viewer.agentKey && !ctx.agent && !ctx.channel`; if !ownerHere && !ctx.ownerConfirmed return `question(viewer, ctx, '

docs/architecture.md, in the same change:
- Section 1 and the diagram: 13 changes -> 14; "7 of the 13 changes start a job" -> "8 of the 14". FLEET node adds "apps kept running on their own ports". The JOBS -> FLEET arrow adds "an app's link: one GET /". HEAL -> RUN covers keep_running via watcher.
- Section 4: "What should be running" gains the writer `keepApp` (five writers), the readers `appNow` and `healApp`, and the app entry shape (`app`, `port`, `memoryGB`, no `model`). "What actually runs" adds containers labelled `spark.app=1`.
- New rule (R37, or the next free number), one row: keep_running is the only way a container that is not a model is started, kept, restarted or stopped. Never on the brain's Spark, for any verb. Never a console model, a model server or a protected container. A new container gets `spark.app=1` (never `spark.console=1`), no GPU, a memory cap, named volumes only, no secret in env, ports bound to 127.0.0.1 and the Spark's tailnet address, and never the model port. A new image runs at once only for the owner on their tailnet with image, port, volumes and env in their own words; otherwise an owner-only button. The 8 GB rule holds for every start (the app's memory figure must fit beyond it; unreadable memory refuses). Done means the app answers at its link, or stays running 15 s when no port is known. It stops nothing to make room. Healing: at most two bring-backs in six hours, after a crash or a stop seen within five minutes of its Spark coming back; a clean stop with the Spark on is held. Check: test/apps.test.mjs.
- One-line touches: R1 (keep_running refuses the brain's Spark), R11 (adopting a running app changes only the list, so no job), R22 (five writers), R25 (`appNamed` is its target check).
- Section 6: "An action" row and checklist item 3 counts 37 -> 38. "A new kind of workload" row: point to keep_running, note that `inventory` now lists every container's state (`containers`), and the yield rule (an app without a GPU is never a stop candidate and never stops anything).
- Section 8: "the other nine change actions" -> ten.
AGENTS.md: both "R1–R36" -> the new last rule number. docs/agent-door.md: a keep_running row in "Actions that change things". test/README.md: a row for apps.test.mjs. docs/code-map.md: regenerate with `node tools/code-map.mjs`.
risk:
- The 8 GB rule is kept strictly, so an app is often refused beside a model that took everything but 8 GB. The refusal says why and what to do; `memoryGB` lets the owner say a smaller figure. After a power cycle an app can stay held for the same reason (list order decides who comes back first).
- The power-cycle tie (a stop seen within five minutes of the Spark coming back) is unverified on a real Spark. It replaces relying on exit 255, because a clean shutdown gives 0, 137 or 143. A power cycle the console did not watch is not healed (same as models today).
- A new image is code running on a Spark that can reach the tailnet as that Spark. That is why it is owner-only, and why there is no way round the button for agents, Telegram, internet sessions or saved steps.
- Qwen may pick stop_model or start_model for an app; those refuse in plain words, and the description, one prompt sentence and the fleet-notes marker point it to keep_running. The real-brain eval must be rerun with the new cases, and the prompt changed by one sentence.
- A new `keep` word kind makes "start X and keep it running" a two-step request (one extra carry-on turn).
- App jobs reuse the deploy, restart and stop types, so the owner's stop of a model on that Spark cancels an app start under way there (it puts back what it did).
- `containers` in inventory comes from `docker ps`; when Docker does not answer, an app reads as "its container is gone" (held, nothing is changed). The planned Docker-ok marker fix should cover this line too.
- An adopted container keeps whatever it was started with (GPU access, host mounts, restart policy); only containers the console starts are fenced.
- Other builders are editing 16-actions, 18-workflows, 19-watcher and architecture.md right now: expect merges, and the tool count may not be 37 when this lands.
- Not run: this spec was written by reading the code; nothing was built or tested.

Re-creating a removed container from a stored spec (the entry is held; the owner names the image again)
GPU for apps the console starts, and any memory or yield rule for GPU apps
A trusted image list, app shelf or per-app templates
Pinning images by digest, and updating an app's image
Host folders, host networking, privileged mode, command or entrypoint override
Secrets in env (no secret store yet)
A separate 'forget' verb (the page's Forget already takes an entry off the list)
Addresses and an answer check for every container in `workloads` (only kept apps get a link)
New job types, event types or page changes
Anything on Spark 2, including a CPU-only budget there
A door beyond the tailnet (Funnel, port 10000, HTTPS links)
Automatic placement: the owner always names the Spark
Immediate crash restart from the watcher (apps come back on the minute pass)

risk:
Low: read only, one argument, no state, no workflow function touched. The build id changes, so `node test/lock.mjs` is needed before install; no workflow version should change (compare `/workflows` before and after).

- The setup match can miss, never mislead. TensorRT-LLM's memory flag is not stripped by `withoutShare`, and a value masked as `[hidden]` breaks equality; both give "no record". A recorded run's setup id is sticky in `recordVerified`, so the wording is "settings are exactly those of setup X", not "was started from X".
- A non-secret flag named like a key shows as `[hidden]` (existing masking).
- Cost: `running_models` already pays an inventory look and a 5-second `/v1/models` probe per model; detail adds one `docker inspect` (20 s limit). Fine under Sparkie's 50-second tool limit on real Sparks; on this Mac the stand-in's inventory alone takes about 20 s, so the new test file runs about 2.5 minutes.
- The `readOutside` check is a text test on the raw arguments (`"detail"`); a false hit only makes memory stricter for that turn.
- Other builders changed 16-actions.mjs, 18-workflows.mjs, 19-watcher.mjs, 20-words.mjs and 25-backup-and-start.mjs while this was written (22:59). The anchors quoted in the spec were still intact at 23:07; re-check them before editing.
- Not verified: the full suite and lock run, real Sparks, a two-Spark model and a llama.cpp model (reasoned from `clusterRunCommand` and `dockerRunCommand`, not run).
- Scratch note: I prototyped in the shared session scratchpad and at first used the names `sc`, `base`, `patch.mjs`, `sc2`, `sc3`, `sc-neg`, `h4` there with `rm -rf` before creating them. If another agent had scratch files under those exact names, they were replaced. Nothing in the project was edited.
